solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Former trucker taking biro from craftsman

indicators.note: taking one thing from another means removing it, so letters are subtracted here
from names the word that the removed letters are taken out of

parts.note: a carpenter is a craftsman in wood
a biro is a ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: A retired lorry driver steals a ballpoint from a tradesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A carter drove a horse-drawn cart carrying goods, an old trade now gone, so a trucker of former times.

clue.text: The sound of that fellow in church

indicators.note: in places the pronoun inside the abbreviation for the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
that fellow is him

explanation.surface: Someone is describing the voice of a man heard inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chime is the ringing sound of bells or a clock, so a sound in general.

clue.text: Greenwood given harsh treatment

parts.note: green, meaning inexperienced, is raw
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Someone named Greenwood has been treated badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname is read as two words; deal is sawn pine or fir boards, a sense less common outside Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw deal is the idiom for unfair or harsh treatment of someone.

clue.text: An overdue reappraisal of venture

indicators.note: a reappraisal looks at the letters again and rearranges them

explanation.surface: A business project is due a fresh assessment that is late in coming.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an attempt or undertaking, the same as a venture.

clue.text: Speed up the Parisian excursion

parts.note: le is French for the
an excursion is a trip

explanation.surface: A tourist is told to hurry along on a Paris outing.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is to go flat out, giving full speed or force.

clue.text: He's going straight to study outside first

indicators.note: first says the second piece named comes at the front of the answer

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, outside
to con is to study, as in conning a text

explanation.surface: Someone heading off directly to read up outdoors before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going straight' is slang for a criminal giving up crime, which is what a former convict does.
explanation.definitionFit: An ex-con is a former prisoner, and one going straight has left crime behind.

clue.text: Sleep at cricket ground leads to dismissal

parts.note: REM is the rapid eye movement phase of sleep
the Oval is a London Test cricket ground

explanation.surface: A cricketer falling asleep during a match gets sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a famous Test cricket ground in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Removal from a post is a dismissal, a sacking.

clue.text: Topless 26, legendary king

parts.note: 26 is the reformer Luther; without its top letter it leaves the first name of King Arthur's father, and the clue wants his surname

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to a mythical British monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the L from 26 (LUTHER) and you have UTHER, the father of King Arthur. The answer is the name that completes his title.
explanation.definitionFit: Uther Pendragon is the legendary British king of Arthurian story, Pendragon meaning chief leader.

clue.text: Hit by small kid's bicycle

parts.note: a trike, or tricycle, is a child's cycle

explanation.surface: Someone was knocked down by a little child's bike.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike is to hit, the verb sense.

clue.text: Prospect of 5-1, win and place

parts.note: five and one in Roman numerals are V and I
an each-way bet, EW, covers both a win and a place

explanation.surface: A punter is weighing a horse at odds of five to one, backed each way.
explanation.walkthrough: 5-1 looks like betting odds but is two Roman numerals; in British betting an each-way bet pays on a win or a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a prospect, the scene looked out upon.

clue.text: Men chatted about task force

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around and reshuffled

explanation.surface: Soldiers chatted about the special unit they belong to.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachment is a unit of troops sent away on a particular mission, like a task force.

clue.text: 18 is one, say, in downward movement

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for say inside the word for kin

parts.note: 18 is SISTER, and a sister is a relation
eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A cross-reference describes something tumbling down.
explanation.definitionFit: Relegation is demotion, especially a sports team dropping to a lower division.

clue.text: She's a bit of a raver actually

indicators.note: a bit of means only part of the following words is taken, the letters lying across them

explanation.surface: A woman is said to be something of a party animal really.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a woman's name, so it fits she in the clue's cryptic grammar.

clue.text: Book government department to accept oil order

indicators.note: accepting something takes it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the FO is the Foreign Office, a UK ministry

indicators.note: putting letters in order rearranges them

explanation.surface: A ministry is told to receive a petroleum delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts the anagram made by 'order' inside the Foreign Office abbreviation; Book is the definition, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a large book made of sheets folded once.

clue.text: Monastic fellow learnt a different way to be brotherly

parts.note: Fra, brother, is the title of an Italian friar

indicators.note: a different way means the letters of learnt are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A monk has found a new way to show kinship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a different way' turns LEARNT into TERNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraternal means like a brother, from Latin frater.

clue.text: Leasing equipment initially to make animal fodder

indicators.note: to make something of letters is to form them into a new word by rearranging
initially takes just the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A farmer rents machinery to produce feed for livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges LEASING into ENSILAG, and 'initially' gives the E of equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensilage is silage, green crops stored and fermented as winter feed for cattle.

clue.text: Browse in Spotify for specific pop genre

parts.note: to surf is to browse, as on the internet
Spotify is a streaming service for music

explanation.surface: A listener scrolls a streaming app looking for a particular style.
explanation.definitionFit: Surf music is a 1960s Californian style of pop and rock associated with the Beach Boys.

clue.text: Fliers follow almost all the ground lights

indicators.note: follow puts the birds after the shortened ground
almost all means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the ground is land, as opposed to sea or air
terns are seabirds, fliers

explanation.surface: Pilots trail nearly the whole airfield's illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanterns are portable lamps, lights carried or hung.

clue.text: Bet on a strict interpretation

indicators.note: an interpretation is a reading of something in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wagers on a narrow reading of the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricast is a wager forecasting the first three finishers in correct order.

clue.text: Someone close threatening to quit home

indicators.note: to quit is to leave, so those letters depart from the longer word

parts.note: sinister means threatening, menacing
in means at home

explanation.surface: A neighbour is menacing to move out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister is a close relative, someone near in family.

clue.text: King's daughter returns to harass the royal

indicators.note: returns means the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: to nag is to harass
ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A princess comes back to pester the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Faux pas involving Irish animal

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a faux pas is a gaffe

explanation.surface: A social blunder concerning a creature from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is an African mammal, so one example of an animal.

clue.text: She's a kind spirit and she's prospering to a degree

indicators.note: to a degree means only partly, so part of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A generous woman is doing rather well.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy or benign spirit of Persian myth, often female.

clue.text: Woman pining for town in Greater Manchester?

parts.note: to miss someone is to pine for them
Marple is a town near Stockport in Greater Manchester

explanation.surface: Someone homesick longs for a northern English town.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Marple is Agatha Christie's elderly spinster sleuth, a famous fictional woman.

clue.text: Signal pioneer sullen before no. 2 love departs

indicators.note: departs means that letter leaves the word built from sullen

parts.note: morose means sullen
love is zero in tennis, O, and no. 2 picks the second of the two such letters

explanation.surface: A gloomy telegraph inventor before his second sweetheart walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Morse pioneered the telegraph and gave his name to Morse code signals.

clue.text: Jeans changed in the middle of Scottish island

indicators.note: changed in the middle means the central letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: Levi's are a brand of jeans

explanation.surface: Someone altered the centre of their denims on a Hebridean isle.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter V of LEVIS becomes a W, a single-to-double U letter swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis is the northern part of the Outer Hebrides island of Lewis and Harris.

clue.text: Discrimination towards brunettes?

parts.note: brunettes are not fair-haired, so prejudice against them is read as a word built of un-, fair and -ness

explanation.surface: Prejudice against dark-haired people.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfairness is injustice or bias, and read literally it is the state of not being fair-haired.

clue.text: The colour of sycophancy

definitions.meaning: the noun is matched with the verb to ..., to flatter servilely

explanation.surface: Asks what shade flattery would be.
explanation.definitionFit: Fawn names a pale brown shade, and as a verb means to toady or grovel.

clue.text: In Tuvalu the real reformer is discovered

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the following words
is discovered says the answer is found there, uncovered among the letters

explanation.surface: A religious reformer turns up in a Pacific island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther led the Protestant Reformation, the archetypal religious reformer.

clue.text: Second small squad held by guards

indicators.note: held by means the squad is gripped between the two letters

parts.note: a crew is a squad or team

explanation.surface: A backup team kept under watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Screws is British prison slang for warders, the guards in a jail.
